01

Two kinds of structure

ABOUT

I am a civil engineer who has spent a decade making physical structures stand up — and the last years building software that makes legacy structures legible.

On site, I have run structure works from excavation to top-out: 20 m diaphragm walls and 50 m piles at Clinique Hannibal 2, the reinforced-concrete frame of the Novotel Lac 2, and a 40-person team delivering the post-tensioned slabs of the Centre de loisir, Lac 2. Since 2021 I run my own company, AZRO Construction.

The through-line is the same in both worlds: respect the existing structure, measure before you claim, and never state more than you can prove. That discipline is what Axiom takes into software — banks and insurers run on COBOL systems nobody fully understands anymore, and “the AI thinks so” is not an answer you can take into a migration decision.

I hold a Diplôme National d’Ingénieur in civil engineering from ENSIT (2015), am a member of the Ordre des Ingénieurs Tunisiens, and work in Arabic, French and English.

02

Axiom

FOUNDER PROJECT — IN DEVELOPMENT

Axiom reads a legacy COBOL estate the way an engineer reads a structure: deterministically, from the source, with every conclusion traced back to the exact lines it rests on.

The analysis itself uses no AI. The engine parses the code and builds its models the same way, every run, so two runs on the same code give the same answer — and a reviewer can check any claim against the source. AI, where it appears at all, only explains results afterwards, and is optional.

P—1

Deterministic by design

Parsing, control-flow and data-flow models, and the semantic layer are computed — not generated. Same input, same output, every time.

P—2

Every claim cites its source

Each fact in an Axiom dossier points to the file and lines it was derived from. If a claim can’t be traced, it doesn’t ship.

P—3

Honest about its limits

The current upgrade teaches the engine to label every fact — proven, bounded, assumed under a named compiler setting, or unknown, with the reason why. The boundary is part of the product, not fine print.

What it does today

  • Parses COBOL programs & copybooks ESTATE-WIDE
  • Control-flow & PERFORM range models CFG
  • Data-flow models & REDEFINES overlap maps DATAFLOW
  • JCL parsing & source-cited dossiers DOSSIER

In the upgrade programme

  • Confidence tags & a boundary register PROVEN / BOUNDED / ASSUMED / UNKNOWN
  • JCL utility semantics — SORT & IDCAMS LINEAGE
  • “Expand this field — what breaks?” CHANGE IMPACT
  • Business-rule extractor, wired into the dossier RULES

Source code is held in private repositories. A walkthrough of the engine and its output is available on request — ask me.
